title: ShipRelay carrier adapter: rates and label purchase
name: Carrier label adapter

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this adapter makes calls to ShipRelay safe to retry? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
ShipRelay responds to a quote request with HTTP 422 and a body describing a bad postal code. What does ShippingCarrier.quote do?
choices: Retries up to maxAttempts times with backoff, then throws an Unavailable CarrierError
Throws a CarrierError of kind InvalidAddress immediately, with no retry
Returns an empty list of quotes
Throws a CarrierError of kind Rejected after one retry

questions.prompt: ShipRelay is overloaded and responds 503 with header 'Retry-After: 0' on every call, with maxAttempts = 3. What does the caller observe?
choices: An immediate throw on the first 503, because Retry-After: 0 means do not retry
Three attempts with no waiting at all between them, then an Unavailable CarrierError
An infinite retry loop, because Retry-After resets the attempt counter
Three attempts separated by exponential backoff with jitter, then an Unavailable CarrierError

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of callers depending on the ShippingCarrier interface rather than on ShipRelayClient directly?
choices: Callers work only with domain types (Address, Quote, cents) and CarrierError kinds, so ShipRelay's wire format, unit conversions, and HTTP details can change or be swapped for another carrier without touching them
It makes every call to ShipRelay faster because responses are cached in the adapter
It guarantees that label purchases are exactly-once regardless of network failures
It lets callers choose per call whether to retry by passing maxAttempts
